scope: Planning only. No learner prose, shared-file edits, Beads writes or Git changes.
method: Fully parsed all 18 active contracts and both actual cumulative registers.
Inspected relevant grammar records and actual learner-master occurrences of pronunciation, orthography, stress, palatal, voicing and syllable terminology.
Traced lexical candidates to existing image-checked records. This audit does not claim fresh source-image inspection or certify new sound values.

existing_related_features.description: Recognize æ, interchangeable manuscript þ/ð, Cook's preference for ð, his hooked ę, and quantity marks; preserve exact printed quantities.
Distinguish long vowels/diphthongs from syllable weight due to two consonants or a geminate; apply only the stated noun-pattern domains.
Complete hof and sǣd patterns; short-stem monosyllabic neuter N/A plural -u versus heavy-stem zero; explain geminates and clusters.
Short/geminated gefręmman and sonorant ęfnan: full finite paradigms, geminate/simple alternation and linking vowel.
Audited dental/sibilant contractions, ð-stem effects, geminate reduction and bounded g/h variants in selected present2/3sg.
Giefan has its checked palatal present and preterite series, including gēafon.
existing_related_features.scope_note: Exact selected lexical series, not a universal ge- prefix or spelling rule.

existing_related_features.description: Biddan, licgan and sittan have j-present geminate patterns, with exact single-consonant present2/3 singulars and their strong pasts.
existing_related_features.scope_note: Present shape alone does not classify the preterite as weak.

existing_related_features.description: Complete selected second-singular/second-plural imperative pairs of weakI–III models, including heavy stems, geminates, short -ian, -rwan, weakII -a/-iað and all four weakIII exceptions.
existing_related_features.scope_note: Morphological production for the declared lexical roster; no new government/complement frame follows for diagnostic lexemes.

course_alignment_findings.finding: The only general sound-related Unit 1 features are recognition-only orthography and syllable weight. The evidence note expressly disclaims a complete reconstructed pronunciation system.
course_alignment_findings.consequence: A guide before Unit 1 must teach all its own sound rules and provide every gloss.

course_alignment_findings.finding: Unit 1 explicitly treats -ginn as the stressed stem in anginn.
course_alignment_findings.consequence: Do not state an absolute first-syllable stress rule. Mark the taught prefix exceptions.

course_alignment_findings.finding: Unit 4 discusses the two written consonants sc only to explain why initial sc does not make scip heavy. It does not establish s+k as a pronunciation.
course_alignment_findings.consequence: The guide can explain two letters representing the usual single sound without revising Unit 4.

course_alignment_findings.finding: Cook spelling, hooked e and macrons are retained. Earlier lessons do not use palatal dots as source spelling.
course_alignment_findings.consequence: Keep original word strings. Any stress bolding, divider or palatal mark must be declared as an editorial aid.

course_alignment_findings.finding: Syllable weight, gemination, vowel quantity and lexical syncope recur in inflection lessons, without teaching a full sound system.
course_alignment_findings.consequence: Do not equate a long vowel with a heavy syllable or a doubled consonant, or invite automatic deletion of unstressed written vowels.

course_alignment_findings.finding: The giefan palatal series has an explicit lexical scope and is not a universal ge- rule.
course_alignment_findings.consequence: Use source-audited word-specific c/g/sc examples and exceptions; the next written vowel alone is not sufficient evidence for every form.

recommended_placement.indexing: Link before Unit 1 in README and course plan; do not renumber the eighteen units or change the Cook assignment crosswalk.
recommended_placement.milestones: Keep all existing chapter and register milestones intact. Record pronunciation outcomes in the guide contract; glossed vocabulary and grammatical meanings are supplied only.

source_convention_coordination.status: Coordinator has selected the working convention; final claims await the source records and contract.
source_convention_coordination.root_message: Cook spellings; Fulk voicing and rounded diphthongs; his permitted traditional short vowels where useful.
source_convention_coordination.scope_response: This is pedagogically coherent if identified plainly as the guide convention and its examples are verified, rather than presented as exact agreement between Cook and Fulk.

proposed_outcomes.scope: Retained letters, thorn/eth equivalence, hooked e, length marks and declared editorial aids.
Selected simple-vowel qualities and length contrasts in printed, glossed examples under the agreed practical convention.
Selected ea/eo/ie and long spellings, with the precise Fulk-based convention and lexical exceptions taught explicitly.
Ordinary consonants plus selected c/g/sc/cg/ng values in the taught words and contexts.
Rounded front vowels, postvocalic h and the relevant non-stop g value using plain articulatory instructions.
Audited f/s/th voicing within the stated sound environments, word boundaries and exceptions.
Distinct vowel and consonant duration, written syllables, and consonant groups without an inserted vowel.
Ordinary word stress and named prefix exceptions; aloud reading of fully supported examples.
The bounded status of the chosen reading convention and practical American English approximations.
Every OE example sense, inflectional meaning and sentence translation; no independent lexical or grammatical production.

presentation.length: Approximately six to eight learner pages and a short separate key, subject to readable complete coverage.
presentation.tables: Current Cambria 10.5-point horizontal-rule style. Three columns: spelling; plain instruction/American cue; glossed OE example. Separate panels rather than a crowded all-in-one chart.
presentation.ipa: Optional once when an unfamiliar sound is introduced. No repeated word transcriptions, feature charts or IPA-memory tasks.
presentation.notes: Keep historical disagreement and source references in endnotes. Put a cue limitation beside the cue when necessary to make it usable.

supported_reading_candidates.reuse: Unchanged reuse of an audited course composition; not a Cook source passage.
supported_reading_candidates.text: Se mann is on ðǣm hofe. Ðæt sǣd is on ðæs mannes hofe. Se fugol is on ðǣm trēowe. Ðæt sǣd is ðæs fugles męte.
supported_reading_candidates.guide_scope: Supply full translation and local pronunciation helps; ask only for oral reading and sound observations. Do not import the grammar/translation questions.

supported_reading_candidates.text: On anginne gescēop God heofonan and eorðan.
supported_reading_candidates.line_convention: First prose line; not an independently printed line number.
supported_reading_candidates.guide_scope: Label as a one-sentence excerpt. Supply the complete meaning and all sound helps. It is contained in the already assigned Unit 1 reading, not a new Cook exercise assignment.
supported_reading_candidates.supplied_translation: In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
supported_reading_candidates.phonetic_support: Exact sound values and stress aids to be supplied by coordinator from the Cook/Fulk source audits; the course glossary alone is not a pronunciation authority.

practice_proposals.proposal: Six to eight printed and glossed words: identify long vowels/diphthongs and doubled consonants, then read without confusing their durations.
practice_proposals.key: Name the exact segment held longer; diagnose the difference between a macron and a doubled consonant.

practice_proposals.proposal: Six taught examples: choose an American English cue or a plain articulatory instruction for c/g/sc/h/y.
practice_proposals.key: State the sound in prose and the relevant context or word-specific exception; require no IPA recall.

practice_proposals.proposal: Four to six image-verified f/s/th examples or pairs: identify the relevant neighbouring sounds and read them.
practice_proposals.key: Separate actual sound environment from spelling and flag exceptions supplied in the guide.

practice_proposals.proposal: Four previously displayed examples, including a named prefix exception: mark stress and preserve written syllables.
practice_proposals.key: Show the stress aid explicitly and diagnose inappropriate modern English reduction or omitted syllables.

practice_proposals.proposal: Read the selected Cook opening sentence with complete meaning and word-specific pronunciation support; make two targeted sound observations. Do not translate or parse independently.
practice_proposals.key: List the actual target sounds and stress points; a written key checks the rule application rather than certifying the reader’s unheard performance.

american_cue_pitfalls.risk: American readers may merge the cue vowels.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Add mouth/lip instructions rather than relying solely on caught or bought.

american_cue_pitfalls.risk: A reader may copy a modern word or letter-name sound rather than the indicated vowel.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Specify the target part of the model word; explain length as duration, with vowel quality taught separately.
american_cue_pitfalls.basis: Editorial teaching design, not a quotation from Cook/Fulk.

american_cue_pitfalls.risk: A modern cue may import a glide into the adopted simple vowel.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Add an explicit steady-vowel/no-glide instruction and distinguish this from the diphthong section.
american_cue_pitfalls.basis: Fulk source editor confirms approximate bait/boat cues in section9.

american_cue_pitfalls.risk: Merely prolonging bit or foot can leave the wrong quality for the chosen long vowel.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Give separate concrete short/long cues as needed. Fulk section19 permits the traditional lax short-vowel convention selected by the coordinator.
american_cue_pitfalls.basis: Fulk source editor reports actual page-image inspection.

american_cue_pitfalls.risk: An unsupported compulsory trill or an unqualified American tap analogy adds avoidable difficulty.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Follow the chosen sources; put optional refinement in a note. If using a tap cue, distinguish it from a trill and qualify regional pronunciation.
american_cue_pitfalls.basis: Fulk source editor reports no compulsory trill in the inspected practical description.

american_cue_pitfalls.risk: Technical aspiration instruction can overwhelm the beginner, and an IPA demonstration is not automatically an OE historical rule.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Omit from required outcomes unless the source reconciliation needs it; otherwise treat as a refinement with an ordinary word cue.
american_cue_pitfalls.basis: Curriculum scope decision; Fulk source editor identifies span/store/score in section9’s IPA introduction.

american_cue_pitfalls.topic: rounded front vowels, postvocalic h, non-stop g
american_cue_pitfalls.risk: Calling a nearby American sound equivalent conceals a difference.
american_cue_pitfalls.handling: Acknowledge the missing ordinary American equivalent and give a concrete articulatory action; optional IPA once.
american_cue_pitfalls.basis: Exact sound values and contexts belong to independent Cook/Fulk source audits.

external_cue_evidence.publication: Authors’ summary of paper1aSC4 at the 158th Acoustical Society of America meeting,26 October2009
external_cue_evidence.inspection: Opened and read the primary research summary; did not play linked audio.
external_cue_evidence.bounded_claim: Its three American speaker examples show both a contrast and mergers, so cot/caught is not a reliable universal American cue pair.
external_cue_evidence.use_limit: Modern English cue design only; not Old English phonological authority.
